messages:
maria_ops: Heads up — eu-north3 seeing a sharp rise in GPU scheduling latency, pending GPU queue up ~3000 in the last 5m. Pod scheduling failing with KV cache errors.
statusbot: Incident created: EU-NORTH3 cache-coordinator fail -> scheduling backlog. Priority: high.
ashley_sre: I can confirm. KV cache coordinator process crashed on several control-plane hosts, eviction storm. Scheduling loop stuck waiting on cache lookups.
devin_infra: Repro: logs show repeated `kv_cache: key not found` followed by OOM-ish backpressure on the scheduler. Rolling restart of coordinator might be required.
maria_ops: Do we have a safe restart plan? We need to avoid cascading evictions that will force mass re-provisioning.
devin_infra: Proposed plan: 1) isolate coordinator on 2 nodes, 2) put read-only proxies in front, 3) roll restarts across AZs. Will take ~30-45m.
leo_neteng: Meanwhile traffic steering to eu-west1 is possible but eu-west1 pools are at 85% reserved capacity. If we push too much, we'll see degraded perf there too.
jen_prod: Can we throttle non-critical customers and prioritize reserved accounts? We should prepare status page language and support notes.
santiago_support: On it. Draft for status page: `We are investigating increased request latency and throttling in EU-NORTH3 due to an internal cache coordinator failure. Some workloads may see slower responses or backlog. We are routing traffic to alternate regions where possible. ETA for mitigation: ~45 minutes.` Thoughts?
maria_ops: Short and action-oriented — add: customers may see higher cost if routed to fallback region (on-demand usage).
santiago_support: Added. Also prepping canned replies for support: list of impacted models, suggestion to reduce batch sizes / lower max_tokens to reduce pressure.
ashley_sre: Quick mitigation we can apply now: reduce max batch size on the scheduler to lower memory pressure, enable aggressive KV TTL to cut stale entries. Deploying patch to config in 2m.
devin_infra: Patch applied to control-plane config on eu-north3 (batch_size: 64 -> 32, kv_ttl: 10m -> 2m). Observed immediate drop in scheduling latency in one AZ.
leo_neteng: Routing update: shifted 22% of traffic to eu-west1 and 8% to apac-edge for overflow. Monitoring downstream latencies.
jen_prod: We're tracking cost impact — FYI finance: short-term on-demand spill will add estimated $6k/hr if sustained. Ops, keep me posted if we need to widen routing.
maria_ops: Noted. Primary fix remains coordinator restart/upgrade. Devin, what's ETA on full restore?
devin_infra: If roll restarts go cleanly, looks like 30-40m. I'll mark progress in the incident bridge.
santiago_support: Status page update pushed (minor wording tweak per Maria). Support queue: flagged customers with reserved contracts and offered free traffic reroute credits where affected.
ashley_sre: After second AZ roll we saw scheduler queue drop from 3k -> 400 in 10m. Still monitoring for regression.
jen_prod: Okay look good. Prep a follow-up status update at +30m even if unchanged.
maria_ops: Good work — keep the bridge open and escalate to on-call infra if rollback needed.
ashley_sre: Bridge link: https://call.redwood/bridge/2261043210
statusbot: Incident update: mitigations applied (config throttle + partial traffic steering). Next update scheduled in 25 minutes.
